cards.judgment: Chile’s Open Finance direction and standardized account-data API documentation are sufficiently grounded in CMF primary materials to support research. The cited account APIs indicate that regulated, consent-based access is technically contemplated, so this is not presently disproven by an unavailable-data/API fatal condition. However, the commercial proposition is an infrastructure-level migration thesis rather than a defined business with demonstrated ability to capture value. The payment-initiation material is described as a consultation/process item, and the supplied record itself identifies a delayed, phased path toward July 2027 and beyond; it should not be treated as immediate, stable production access. A new entrant also faces potentially material licensing, security, consent, privacy, AML, operational-resilience, certification, and dispute-handling obligations. Those costs may be rational for a focused, regulated use case with proprietary distribution or risk/workflow advantage, but there is no evidence yet that standalone aggregation/orchestration economics justify them. Therefore it survives as HQ-worthy research, conditional on narrowing to a customer-validated use case and confirming the applicable regulatory perimeter and production-access path.
